sn48.58:1.1: This is famously the scene of Sāriputta’s awakening ([mn74:1.2]()).
sn48.58:1.3: The interpretation of this discourse is problematic, and no parallels are recorded. However, I believe it is thematically similar to [sn16.5](), where Mahākassapa explains that he continues his austere lifestyle even though he is enlightened both because he enjoys it, and to inspire future generations. | I take the expression _pavattamāno pavattati_ (“in rolling forth, roll forth”) as referring to Sāriputta’s role as the disciple who, like no other, continues to “roll forth” the wheel of the teaching ([mn111:23.1](), [sn8.7:3.4](), [an1.187:1.1]()). The Buddha is asking what motivates Sāriputta to teach.
sn48.58:1.4: Presumably this means so that others can realize awakening.
sn48.58:2.2: The text seems corrupt here, as first, the faculties are the path to awakening, not awakening itself, and second, an arahant does not “develop” for they have already fully developed. “Develop” (_bhāveti_) is a causative verb, to “make be more”. Such verbs can mean to make or instigate someone to do something, although this is not how this very common verb is used elsewhere. Nonetheless, the sense here seems to be that an arahant teaches in order to establish others on the path to awakening.
sn48.58:3.2: Five things leading to non-decline of the dispensation.
